title: Throughput Lighthouse: lightweight TPS microbenchmark suite for core models
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a small, reliable microbenchmark suite (the "Throughput Lighthouse") that teams can run locally and in CI to measure tokens-per-second (TPS) and tail latency (p95/p99) for our core served models. The suite should be lightweight, reproducible, and capture steady-state throughput, microburst behavior, and KV-cache warm vs cold scenarios. It must produce machine-readable artifacts (JSON) and human-readable summaries for dashboards and regression detectors.

Why: Current ad-hoc TPS tests vary by harness and environment. We need a canonical, easily auditable baseline that: 1) reduces noise across runs, 2) provides deterministic inputs for regression alerts, 3) is cheap to run in CI and nightly, and 4) clearly separates workload shapes (short chat bursts, long completions, prefix-heavy sequences).

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: lightweight JVM/Python harness that invokes internal inference endpoint or local runtime; sample distributions (short/medium/long); KV cache warm/cold toggles; measurement of TPS, median, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, variance, and steady-state slope; output JSON artifact with metadata (model, runtime config, kernel flags, sequence length distribution).
- Out of scope: full-scale stress tests (handled by other load farms), complex multi-tenant simulations, conformance tests for customer protocols.

Design notes:
- Workloads: three canonical workload shapes: 
  1) Short-chat: 8-16 tokens per response, high request rate.
  2) Medium-completion: 64-256 tokens, moderate rate.
  3) Long-stream: 512+ tokens, focused on throughput-tail behavior and KV cache effects.
- Warm vs cold KV: run paired experiments where one run populates the KV cache (prefix replay) and one run intentionally cold-starts caches to measure penalty.
- Sampling: run N warmup iterations (configurable, default=10), then M measurement iterations (default=100) and compute sliding-window TPS to detect warmup completion.
- Statistical detection: compute baseline medians and p95 across runs and apply a regression rule: alert when median TPS drops >10% vs baseline AND p95 increases by >5% absolute or relative (configurable thresholds). Also support control-chart style drift detection for long-term trends.
- Artifact schema: flat JSON fields: run_id, model, runtime_version, config_flags, sequence_profile, mean_tps, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, sample_count, timestamp. These names should be stable so downstream regression detectors and dashboards can parse them.
- CI integration: small smoke job (quick) for pre-merge (runs short-chat shape with 20 iterations) and a nightly job with full shapes to refresh baselines. Use self-hosted runners that have pinned GPU/CPU config to reduce variance.

Acceptance criteria:
- A runnable repo/harness under infra/benchmarks/lighthouse with a README and example run commands.
- JSON artifact schema documented and validated by the harness.
- CI jobs added: lighthouse-smoke (pre-merge, < 5 minutes) and lighthouse-nightly (full suite, configurable).
- Regression detector reads artifacts and raises alerts into Ops when thresholds are crossed; initial alerting rules present in prometheus/ops-runbook.
- Example baseline artifacts for 3 core models checked into artifacts/baselines with tags.

Instrumentation and telemetry:
- Emit structured JSON and a minimal Prometheus metrics endpoint for each run (for dashboards).
- Include tags for model name, quantization profile, kernel variant, and batch settings.
- Correlate runs with git commit and runtime image tag.

Operational considerations:
- Keep run cost low: default nightly runs limited to one machine per model and short/medium/long shapes sampled (total run ~45 minutes).
- Seed sequences stored in repo with test vectors derived from real workloads (anonymized).
- Provide a utility to replay a specific failing run locally (repro tool).

Deliverables:
- harness code + README + unit tests.
- JSON artifact validator and example outputs.
- CI job definitions and initial baselines checked in.
- Integration plan for regression-detector (provide schema and example data).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Canary harness runs locally and in CI producing validated JSON artifacts.
2) Nightly job refreshes baseline artifacts for three core models and publishes to artifacts/baselines.
3) Regression detector ingests artifacts and can trigger a PagerDuty alert when thresholds are crossed.
4) README contains run recipes (local, containerized, ci) and troubleshooting steps.
5) PR with code + tests + CI settings merged and smoke job green.

2025-11-24 — PM review (Rosa Kim): Confirmed customer impact is high for dedicated customers; requested exportable CSV for audits. Adding CSV support to artifact outputs.
2025-11-28 — Design feedback (Marta Ruiz): Suggested adding visual diffs for p95 histograms in the nightly report. We'll add a small HTML report generator as optional output.
